title: Probability of Repeated Uniform Sampling
statement: Let $N,k\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $P$ be any property of optional natural numbers. Put $L=\mathrm{size}(N-1)$, where subtraction is truncated at zero. The probability that the procedure which reads $k$ consecutive blocks of $L$ random bits, returns the first block value less than $N$, and returns no value if there is none satisfying this condition, produces an output satisfying $P$ equals $1/2^{kL}$ times the number of tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\in\{0,\ldots,2^L-1\}^k$ for which the first $a_t<N$ exists and $P$ holds of that first such value, or for which no such $a_t$ exists and $P$ holds of no value.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a property of optional natural numbers
